q: A graph of photosynthesis rate against light intensity rises steadily, then levels off into a plateau. What does the plateau show?
options: The plant has reached the highest rate of photosynthesis it could achieve under any conditions
Light is no longer limiting; another factor, such as CO2 or temperature, now limits the rate
Light intensity is still the limiting factor, but its effect has become smaller
The chlorophyll has been destroyed by the high light, so the rate can't rise further
explanation: By the law of limiting factors, the rate is set by the factor in shortest supply. On the rising part, light limits: more light, faster rate. On the plateau, more light has no effect, so something else – usually CO2 concentration (Rubisco's substrate) or temperature (enzyme activity) – is limiting. Raising that factor would raise the plateau. Damage from excess light would cause a decline, not a flat plateau.
